answer: Verifiable-delay minting resists sybils: forging a key requires a sequential delay function, work no parallel hardware can shortcut, each pulse of computation following the last. This sets an irreducible wall-clock floor per identity, so a swarm either waits serially or buys proportional hardware to run an orchard of delays at once. Either way mass minting costs real time or real machines, never a free burst. The latency is a pigment hardware cannot bleach out. Precondition: the function is fast to verify, slow to compute.
